# Working on this repository

<!-- kit:constitution begin (generated by `kit agent-guard sync` from constitution.rules.json: never edit by hand) -->
## Constitution (one registry: `constitution.rules.json`; every rule below is also enforced by hooks, `kit check canon` and CI)

- **Diagrams come only from kit diagrams render.** Every diagram is produced by `kit diagrams render` from a Mermaid source that carries the `%% kit:diagram` header (kit.diagram.v1) and the project's theme. Never a hand-made PNG or SVG, never mmdc, Kroki, mermaid.live or any other renderer.
- **Every diagram is stored as source and PNG with an index.** Each diagram shown anywhere is committed as source plus PNG under docs/diagrams/ with the generated index; the PNG must match its source. Run `kit diagrams render`, never edit the index.
- **Show the rendered image and look at it first.** Show the rendered image itself in the conversation, and look at it before sending or committing it: font loaded, nothing clipped or overlapping, readable at phone width. *(instruction only: nothing can force it)*
- **Every architecture or design description includes a diagram.** Every architecture or design description (docs, README, PR description, reply) includes a Mermaid diagram, not only text or tables, and a change to how pieces fit together updates docs/ARCHITECTURE.md in the same change. *(instruction only: nothing can force it)*
- **Generated files are never hand-edited.** A generated file is never edited by hand: change its source and run its generator (kit vendor sync, kit claude sync, kit diagrams render, kit widgets build, kit sdk generate). The vendored kit under vendor/kit is changed in the kit repository only.
- **Schema first, contract first, canonical.** Nothing is hardcoded: every API, webhook, event, email template, MCP tool and plugin has an OpenAPI 3.1 or JSON Schema 2020-12 contract proven by tests; every config, content and data file is schema-validated; one source per fact.
- **Never write, read or print a secret.** Never write a secret into a file, a command, a commit or a message; never read a secret file (.env, .dev.vars, keys) or print an environment variable that holds one. Secrets live in the environment of the platform that needs them. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **Never skip hooks, force-push or push to a protected branch.** Never use --no-verify, never switch git hooks off, never force-push, never push straight to main or master, and never change rulesets or branch protection. Fix the failing check instead.
- **The enforcement itself is never disabled.** Never edit .claude/settings*.json or the hook files to weaken them, never set disableAllHooks, and never start `claude` with --bare, --safe-mode, --setting-sources or --settings. Changes to enforcement are made by the owner, in the kit.
- **A subagent writes only inside its declared scope.** A subagent writes only inside the scope declared for its agent type in constitution.rules.json (read-only agents write nothing). An agent type with no declared scope may not write; declare it, do not work around it.
- **kit check canon runs first; nothing deploys untested.** `kit check canon` is the first step of npm test, every pull request runs npm test in CI, and every deploy script runs the tests first. A red run is fixed, never waived, baselined or skipped.
- **Every resource carries its project's name as prefix.** Every resource a project owns is prefixed with the project's own name, as the project registry (packages/core/registry/projects.json) lists it; never a retired prefix. One resource serves one project. Before deleting anything: check routes, domains and bindings, archive to R2 and a GitHub archive branch. *(instruction only: nothing can force it)*
- **Portable parts belong in the kit.** Portable code, schemas and checks belong in SaasReport/kit; a site keeps its own content, brand and config, never edits the kit in the site; holds it at its head (t=0). *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **The author never deploys or changes production.** An agent that writes code never deploys it and never changes production state (wrangler deploy, secrets, remote D1, DNS or Cloudflare API writes). Open a pull request; the reviewed CI environment deploys. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **Deploys run in a CI environment, not from a machine.** Production changes only through the one production workflow (kit release, docs/RELEASE.md): main's HEAD, a GitHub environment, the tested build, each D1 migrated first; every Worker answers /api/build with its commit. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **A monitor always names who it tells, and never in git.** Every alert route a monitor declares resolves at run time (binding, template, a well-formed destination) or the monitor refuses to run. Recipients are Worker secrets the owner sets, never in git, never empty: one owner address, info@<domain>, set by the deploy (kit release ship). *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **Only the owner approves and merges.** An agent never approves, merges or enables auto-merge of a pull request, its own or anyone's, and never writes an approval row (fa-review, merge authority, native-reader approval). The owner principal approves and merges. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **Every failover and restore is proven by a recorded drill.** A backup, a fallback sender, a second DNS root or a restore path counts only with a dated drill record that passed; a mitigation with no drill is not a mitigation. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **Every deployed Worker is watched.** Every wrangler config this repository deploys (found by content, every [env.*]) is watched by a monitor declared in resilience.json, or is that monitor.
- **A monitor writes to a database it does not watch.** A monitor Worker binds its own D1; by database_id (names resolved), it differs from every D1 the watched Workers bind, and MONITOR_DB_ID and MONITOR_WATCHED_DB_IDS carry those ids so the monitor refuses at run time too.
- **A stale status is reported as stale.** stale_after_min is at least the longest gap between the monitor's cron firings and at most three of them; a status older than that, or dated in the future, is stale, never passing.
- **The absence of a monitor is reported by an independent path.** A scheduled GitHub watcher (kit resilience watch, kept alive by kit resilience keepalive) and, for a worker monitor, a dead-man provider on another root report the absence; the ping result is stored and a failed ping fails the run.
- **Every alert route is proven every day.** At least two routes on two roots; the canary goes through every route once a day and each delivery is recorded; a route that fails is alerted through the others and fails the run; the watcher fails on a stale route or a failed delivery.
- **Every D1 and R2 has a backup in another resource.** Every D1 database and R2 bucket a watched Worker binds has a backup whose destination is a different resource, driven by a backup config, with a restore drill.
- **Signing keys are not held by whoever can deploy.** Signing keys live in a KMS or HSM with threshold holders who are not the deployers; a public key set exposes production keys only. *(instruction only: nothing can force it)*
- **One decision path at every boundary.** Every boundary an agent action passes (prompt, tool call, agent spawn and stop, commit, push, pull-request merge, CI, deploy, network egress) is decided by the same rules, then the tighten-only advisors, through the resident daemon, and holds when the daemon cannot answer. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **No process outlives its task.** Every process an agent or the guard starts is bounded: `claude -p` runs under `timeout` or --max-turns, a detached process under `timeout`, every hook has a timeout, every CI job a timeout-minutes, and the decision daemon exits when idle, when old and when its project is gone.
- **No orphan branch, worktree or pull request.** A worktree whose directory is gone, a branch already merged, an agent branch with no upstream and no commits for weeks, and an open pull request with no activity are orphans: finish, merge or delete them. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **No stored object without a record.** Every stored object (an upload, a backup, an export) has exactly one record, and every record has its object; the two lists are reconciled and the difference is an orphan. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **No generated artefact without a source.** Every generated file (a diagram image, the vendored kit, an SDK, a generated agent or block) has its source and its generator; an artefact whose source is gone, or that was edited by hand, fails the canon.
- **No rule without an enforcing gate, no gate without a rule.** Every rule names the layers that enforce it, and every enforcing hook or check is claimed by a rule: a claim with nothing behind it, or an enforcer no rule owns, fails the canon.
- **An agent never mints, revokes or sets a credential.** An agent never creates, rotates, revokes or sets a token, secret or deploy credential (Cloudflare tokens, wrangler or GitHub secrets). Scoped deploy credentials are issued by the governed custody path, never ad hoc. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **Infrastructure mutations are declared actions, decided first.** Every external or infrastructure mutation (Cloudflare, GitHub administration, DNS, tokens, secrets, deploys) is a declared action class in the registry, decided by the same path before it happens, and an agent cannot perform it directly; each refusal leaves an evidence record. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **Nothing merges without the owner's review.** A pull request merges only after the owner has reviewed it, with the required checks green; an agent never merges its own or any pull request, and never enables auto-merge. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **Only declared tools run.** Every tool an agent can call belongs to a declared class (read, exec, write, network, agent, meta) or is an MCP tool of a listed server; anything else is held until the owner declares it.
- **Commands are written out, not hidden.** A command is written out where the guard can read it: no decoded string run as a command, no command named by a variable, no shell fed from a pipe or a download, no script written and run in one command, no inline interpreter code that starts processes. *(only part of this can be forced)*
- **Every agent commit is attributable to its own key.** Each agent acts as a kit principal (kit:agent:<trust-domain>:<kind>:<local>) with its own signing key; its commits carry a signed trailer, and a commit by an agent with no key is held, so the guard can tell an agent's work from the owner's.
